evidence:
_resolve_branch_tip() is a verbatim extraction of the tip-resolution logic previously inlined in audit_branch_tips(): same source order (local refs/remotes/origin/
^{commit} -> ls-remote refs/heads/
), same HEX40 gate, same fail-closed die. Only the die message gained a `where` prefix. Both layers now call one implementation.

declared_branch_tip() is a thin wrapper differing only in cache dict. The cache split is justified: audit_branch_tips() short-circuits on `if _AUDIT_TIPS: return _AUDIT_TIPS`, so a shared dict populated first by a non-standard branch would skip resolution of the two canonical branches.
Branch namespace check on the top-level field was tightened from startswith('audit/landing-') to the same _AUDIT_BRANCH_NS regex H-3 uses.
MEASURED: git merge-base --is-ancestor fed3e70ba8430e0fad4f27df11d2eca550f33d30 refs/remotes/origin/audit/landing-adversarial -> 0 (YES). Legitimate grant still passes; no regression.

MEASURED: local remote-tracking refs match ls-remote exactly for both audit branches (origin/audit/landing-adversarial=a97daeb..., origin/audit/landing-ssot=bc1a612...), so the local-ref-first resolution order is not returning a stale tip in the current repo state.

findings.statement: residual_in_force() passes accepted_by_audit_report to `git show <a_sha>:<rep_path>` with no path validation of any kind. H-3's reports_at() by contrast enumerates every .json under research/landing_accessibility/audit/ in the commit tree, and its docstring states the design principle explicitly ('the ledger does not get to choose the path'). With ancestry now closed, the choice of which file counts as the audit adjudication still rests with the ledger.

findings.risk_condition: Becomes material if the lineages are ever merged (e.g. an audit branch rebased onto or merged from main).
findings.remediation: Constrain rep_path to ^research/landing_accessibility/audit/.*\.json$, or better, reuse reports_at(a_sha) and scan the whole subtree — the latter is the true structural analogue of H-3.

findings.statement: abrr_grant_hits() hits if any site in the document affirms the id, with no precedence between sites. A document carrying REJECT at one node and ACCEPT_RECLASSIFY at another for the same id yields a hit regardless of which is the draft and which is the conclusion.

findings.remediation: Deferred with L-1. Any fix should treat both functions together.
